title: Infant COVID-19 Risk w/ Unvaccinated Family Members
selftext:
My wife and I are vaccinated and boostered. We have a six-month old son and have been planning for several months to attend Christmas in Northern Indiana with my family (we live on the West Coast).  About half of my family is anti-vaccination and they have been operating without restrictions for a long time now. When we bought our tickets, cases were low and we figured that with low risk to children, this Christmas would be the time to accept the situation and reconnect with everyone.

Currently, however, Indiana is in the midst of a massive COVID spike. We asked our pediatrician for advice on this trip and she recommended against it, citing some indication of special problems (concerning chest xrays) for children under age one and some "concerning early data" on Omicron. She also said that vaccine authorization for 6 months+ is likely in the next 2-3 months and asked if we could wait until then. We got a second opinion from another pediatrician (family friend) and this doctor said the chances of anything really bad happening to our baby are extremely low and that attending is not clearly a wrong decision.

We are not sure what to do. Speaking with the family about a potential middle ground of us flying in but not attending the main gatherings and not staying with my parents (who are 70 and unboostered 8 months after J&J) made it clear that it would be better for everyone if we simply postponed rather than arrive and stay distanced. The family gathering is likely to be about 25 people, mix of adults and kids over 5, in a very tight environment.

Not attending is clearly the safest option but at this point we are also concerned about negative effects on family relationships. This may be the only chance most family members have to see the baby while he is still really a baby. In some ways this situation feels like two types of irrationality (us worried about extremely low chances of something happening to our child, and family members worried about some theoretical vaccine risk).

We are trying to untangle this risk and looking for any input or further perspective that will help us make the stay/go decision. Thank you!

selftext:
38 Male Ohio


**UPDATE** # 2

Original:


My husband takes Lacosamide for seizures caused by scar tissue from a right frontal meningioma resection in June 2020.

I am at a loss about what to do and I am freaking out because the last time my husband had seizures, he went into status epilepticus and had to be placed in a medically induced coma for two days.


Please, what else can we do to obtain his medication by tonight? The pharmacies close at 6 p.m. EST. It is now noon.

title: Question about some heart palpitations. Want additional information to give cardiologist if possible.
selftext:
Age: 23

Sex: male

Height: 6'0

Weight: ~148

Location: Florida, U.S.

Race: White

Medications: No prescriptions, just OTC allergy meds and heartburn meds.

Hey there, so I'll just jump right into this. I was getting setup at the doctor after moving today, and mentioned that I have been having some very minor basically symptom-less heart palpitations. These feel like skipped beats basically. I'll feel my heart beating normally, then a slight pause, followed by a harder beat. I've had these for a while now, and am pretty sure they are just benign PVC's. I have no symptoms of any heart issue, or no family history of heart issues. The only thing I can note is I have a slightly fast heart rate when working out however I attribute this to me being out of shape and getting back into a routine.

In addition to this I am to get some blood work done but it's nothing out of the ordinary. Just the usual: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, CBC (includes diff / PLT), lipid panel, and TSH/reflex to FT4.

So that's the backstory. I was just curious if you all had any other opinions, or had anything I should bring up with the cardiologist or my PCP when I see them again. Just want to make sure I hit all of my bases and get the most out of these visits.

title: 37M Diagnosed Brain Tumor/Mass - Need Help Navigating
selftext:

Is there a surgeon that I should absolutely seek treatment from, particularly one in my region? Please, if anyone has any POSITIVE feedback and anecdotal outcomes, I'd love to hear it. I'm spiraling and am terrified because everything I have read about brain tumors seems incredibly grim, and I have a young daughter and wife who rely on me.

Thank you.

title: For my Brother, Neurologist's staff dropped the ball. Now how do I complain to the Doctor, and help my Brother get care in a different state?

Neurologist's State: Virginia

My Brother's Age: 40

Gender: Male

Weight: about 200 lbs

Location: Head

Duration: Years

Medical History: Migraines/Headaches, ADHD, PTSD

Current Meds: Vyvanse for ADHD, and trying to figure out the rest

Health Insurance: Obamacare plan - Tufts Health Together


**BACKGROUND:**  My Brother was getting sub-standard care from Neurology Nurse Practitioners in Boston for his mental health and headaches/migraines. (For example, first NP would give him ADHD meds, then would leave the practice, and the new one would abruptly cut him off, and switch him to anti-depression meds). **TIMELINE:** My Neurologist evaluated my brother, and gave him an overview of what he thinks it's going on, as well as a plan moving forward by trying different meds. **NOW WHAT?** My brother is upset - he's been left hanging, and paid a few thousand dollars for these appts (out of pocket).  I'm going to see the Neurologist next week. Thanks.

title: 10 yr old diagnosed with E. coli 0157:H7
selftext:
My 10 year old daughter has been having ongoing diarrhea with stomach cramps and unusual for her tiredness off and on for a few months now. We kind of thought maybe she had irritable bowel syndrome like her dad has so we took her to the pediatrician. 

To be honest at first I just thought she was getting stomach bugs from school until the 3rd or 4th time which is why it went on so long. 

Her pediatrician ordered Blood and fecal tests and found that she carried the E. coli 0157:H7 strain but for the life of me I can’t figure out where she got it. She doesn’t eat meat (it’s a strain cattle carries) or salad (current outbreaks of romaine had this) since she has a sensory disorder. 

Apparently this strain can’t be treated with antibiotics because it produces the shiga toxin which is a. Deadly and b. Can cause hus which can cause kidney failure and she would either need dialysis or a transplant. 

We don’t see a gastroenterologist for 2 weeks. The two ua’s she’s had show trace blood in her urine. 

I’m just not finding any information anywhere on treatment options since antibiotics will cause the E. coli bacteria to shed the shiga toxin and cause her condition to get worse. So now I’m checking the toilet every time she goes and her toilet paper for blood to catch it before it gets serious cause that’s the only information our pediatrician could give us. 

I’m trying to stay positive but it’s really hard, she’s my baby and she’s not doing good. Does anyone have experience with this and know of treatment options? I live in a small town in Kansas with few specialists in the area.

title: Filling an out-of-state prescription on vacation
selftext:
Hey all. I’m having some trouble filling a prescription and am looking for advice (I apologize if this is the wrong sub for this; it looked like the best place since r/pharmacy doesn't allow these types of posts).

I’m currently on vacation in Massachusetts, and have a 30-day Adderall prescription from out-of-state that I need to fill (IL, if that matters). I attempted to fill it the other day, and was informed of a new law here mandating that out-of-state prescriptions for Schedule II substances can only be filled within five days of the start date. The prescription is around a month old (I was given two 30 day prescriptions last time I saw my doctor) so they were unable to fill it.

The pharmacist said my doctor may be able to send a new prescription either electronically or via mail, or that I could try going to an urgent care facility with the prescription and explaining my situation to them. Unfortunately, my doctor told me she won’t be able to send a new prescription. She recommended going to urgent care as well, or having someone fill it for me in IL and then mailing it to me.

Do I have any other options here? I’m a bit wary of going to urgent care, since that would probably be a huge process and there’s a good chance I’ll either come back with nothing or a partial fill, and I’ll be here for almost another month. I may be able to have someone in IL fill it for me, but that would also be a hassle, and would require waiting a week or more for my meds. I could also possibly try to fill it in New Hampshire since I'm fairly close, but I’m not sure that I'd fare any better with the laws there. This also could be pretty difficult because there are only a select few pharmacies I can go to out of state due to my insurance.

Any help would be appreciated. Thanks in advance.

title: My wife's severe stomach problem, lasting over a month now...
selftext:
Hello everyone,

My wife has been having the worst month of her life. 

She’s 31 years old, Female 5'07 185lbs Brazilian. This has been going on for more than a month now. We live in Revere, Massachusetts. She has no existing medical conditions other than this vomiting and nausea and is currently taking Famotidine and Prilosec, prescribed by her PCP and GI Doctor.  She has never smoked cigarettes but does use a nicotine vape.

It started about a month ago with her initially feeling some nausea, then it got better for a few days, then she woke up one morning and was viciously vomiting to the point of dry heaving stomach bile for almost 2 weeks, she’ll feel better, then start having these intense vomiting and dry heaving stomach bile episodes, then she’ll feel better snd now tonight she’s having another episode which has now turned in to about a month with her having these horrible nausea snd vomiting episodes. It’s like a belching dry heaving where it sounds like she’s burping while her body is trying to vomit and it’s just stomach bile. She’s now taken medical leave from work because of this.

We have gone to the ER 4 different times, had mobile IV nurses come 3 times and give her fluids, vitamins and anti-nausea and anti-inflammatory medications which seemed to give her some relief temporarily. We’ve contacted her PCP, had an appointment with a GI specialist, they did a CT Scan, Ultrasound, blood, urine and stool samples all came up negative. White blood cell count was 9.3 so on the high end but normal? She has an endoscopy scheduled for October 6th which was the earliest appointment we were able to get after her PCP put in an urgent endoscopy order, but that’s still 3 weeks from now. so we’ll see what happens with that but I just wanted to see if any professionals on here could offer any help, advice, theories, anything would be appreciated.

Today she didn’t eat all day but then when she came come she was hungry and went out to a restaurant with her mom and had some rice, beans and fried fish and immediately started feeling chills and nausea, more than nausea, she’s constantly moaning in pain and she says it feels like her stomach is being eaten alive from the inside, feeling a strong pulsing inside.

They have her on Famotidine and Prilosec which she takes daily but she’s currently not able to hold down any food or liquids so she usually just puked up the medication as well. We’re currently at an Urgent care center where they’re giving her IV Famotidine and ZOFRAN but she is still feeling bad.

She hasn’t been drinking or smoking cannabis since this all stared. Before it started she did consume alcohol and cannabis and initially we thought it could be CHS because of what we’ve read about the illness but it’s been a month now with no cannabis so I don’t think that’s it.

They haven’t given her any antibiotics which I was curious about. I believe because the blood work tested for parasites and that came up negative and her white blood cell count was within range but I was curious if maybe IV antibiotics would be worth trying. The doctors at this urgent care we’re at now don’t seem to think so but they did do blood work so maybe if they see something new in her blood they will, I don’t know.

I’ve read up on Cyclical Vomiting which it definitely seems like she has all the symptoms of, I just don’t know what to do. We’ve had her on a mostly gluten and dairy free diet but haven’t been perfect with it. Like last night she had a non dairy ice cream but with a cone so that’s gluten.! She was craving something sweet.

If anyone has anything they can recommend or guide us in any way or just any help at all would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you in advance.

\-Stephen and Raisa
